collected_dynamic_variables.call_volume: Around 30 calls a week hit voicemail
collected_dynamic_variables.pain_points: Calls going to voicemail; Missed callers not leaving messages; Worried it's an AI scam/gadget; Data privacy/access concerns; Concern about outbound calls without consent

transcript:
User: Yeah I saw your thing online. Honestly this smells like one of those AI scam gadgets. Convince me it's not garbage.
Agent: Totally fair—there’s a lot of “AI” junk out there. When a new customer calls you and you can’t pick up, what happens right now—does it go to voicemail or does someone answer?
User: It goes to voicemail, but who listens to those anymore? How do I know this isn't recorded?
Agent: Yeah, exactly—most people don’t leave a message, so the lead just disappears. On the “recorded” worry: are you asking if the system is just playing a canned message instead of actually handling the caller live?
User: Exactly. And who gets to see my data? I don't want just anyone accessing my business information.
Agent: Makes sense—ours isn’t a canned recording; it answers live and captures the caller’s details so you can follow up, and access to your info is restricted to you and anyone you authorize. What kind of business is this for?
User: It's for a roofing business, but how do I know this isn't some robot calling my customers without my consent?
Agent: Got it—roofing makes a ton of sense for this. We don’t have it calling anyone unless you explicitly turn on outbound follow-ups; the default is just answering inbound calls to your number when you miss them. Roughly how many calls a week hit voicemail for you?
User: Around 30 calls hit voicemail weekly. But why should I trust your system with my business?
Agent: I hear you—trust is the whole thing. Practically, you stay in control: it only answers calls that come to your number, it collects the exact info you decide (like address, roof type, storm damage), and only you/your authorized users can access it.  

When those ~30 calls go to voicemail, do you think even half of them would’ve booked an inspection if someone answered live?
User: Maybe, maybe not. But prove to me this isn't just another scheme before I even consider it.
Agent: Totally fair—rather than asking you to “believe” anything, we can keep it grounded in what you can verify: if it answers missed inbound calls live and you see the caller details/recording in your own log, it’s real; if it doesn’t, you drop it.  

Has anyone ever showed you the math on what those ~30 voicemail calls a week could be costing you?
User: Yeah, 30 calls. But who's doing the math here? How do I know you're not bluffing?
Agent: Good question—no bluffing, we only use your numbers and you can sanity-check it in one line.  

Of those 30 missed calls a week, what percent do you think would actually book if someone answered—10%, 25%, 50%?
User: Alright, I'd say around 40% would book if someone answered. But still, how do I know this isn't a scam?
Agent: Got it—40% helps. To keep this real, the math is only your inputs; last piece: what’s your average job value, roughly—are we talking $5,000, $10,000, $15,000?
User: It's around $1,800 per job. But I'm still not convinced this isn't some kind of scam.
Agent: Makes sense. Using your numbers: 30 missed calls/week × 40% booking × $1,800 is about **$21,600/week**, or roughly **$93,500/month** slipping through voicemail.  

It’s a 20-minute walkthrough—Jay will show you exactly how it answers and what you can control around data and outbound. What’s better for you—later today or tomorrow?
User: Fine, tomorrow works. But I'm still wary. This better not be a waste of my time.
Agent: Got it—I’ll keep it tight and useful. What time tomorrow is best for you?
User: Alright, let's aim for 3 PM. But remember, I'm skeptical — this better be worth it.
Agent: Fair—and 3 PM works. Before I lock in the right 3 PM, what time zone are you in: Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
User: I'm in Central Time. Don't want any mix-ups, so make sure it's the right 3 PM.
Agent: Perfect—**3:00 PM Central**, tomorrow. What’s your first name?
User: Just call me Sam. And make sure you got my number right: +14695550001. No games.
Agent: Got it, Sam—and yep, I have **+1 469-555-0001** on file. What’s your last name?
User: Ortiz. But just stick to the roofing talk. I'm still keeping my guard up, you know?
Agent: Totally hear you, Sam. What’s the name of your roofing company?
User: Ortiz Roofing. But remember, I'm still skeptical about this whole deal. Don't try anything funny.
Agent: Got it, Ortiz Roofing—and I hear you on the skepticism. Tomorrow I can do **3:15 PM** or **4:00 PM Central**; which works?
User: Let's go with 3:15 PM Central. But remember, I'm still on high alert for any nonsense.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Hang tight one second—my calendar’s being picky, I’m re-confirming it now.
Agent: I’m having trouble confirming the calendar for **3:15 PM Central** on my end right now. I can try another slot—does **4:00 PM Central tomorrow** work?
User: Sure, but I'm not holding my breath. Let's see if this is really worth my time.
Agent: Got it, Sam—let’s do **4:00 PM Central tomorrow (Wednesday, Aug 26)** instead. Want me to lock that one in?
User: Fine, 4:00 PM Central tomorrow works. But I'm still suspicious, so this better impress me.
Agent: One moment while I lock in 4:00 PM Central for tomorrow.
Agent: I’m seeing a formatting issue with the phone number on my end—even though it looks right as **+1 469-555-0001**. Can you confirm the number exactly as **+14695550001** is the best one for the call?
User: Alright, but remember, I'm not convinced yet. This call better be straight and to the point.
Agent: Totally—Jay will keep it straight and to the point. Quick confirm: is **+14695550001** the best number for the call?
User: Yeah, that's the right number: +14695550001. But remember, I’m still wary, so keep it honest.
Agent: Got it, Sam—appreciate it, and we’ll keep it honest and roofing-specific. I’ve got **4:00 PM Central tomorrow (Wed, Aug 26)** set for Ortiz Roofing; is there anything else you want Jay to focus on—privacy/access controls, or making sure it never does outbound without consent?
User: Privacy and control are priorities. No outbound without my say-so. Let's see if this really works.
Agent: Got it—privacy and tight control, and **no outbound unless you explicitly turn it on**. For tomorrow at **4:00 PM Central**, Jay will walk you through the exact access controls and outbound settings—anything else you want him to bring up?
User: No, that's it. Just ensure it's straightforward and no hidden tricks. I'll be ready at 4:00 PM Central.
Agent: Thanks, Sam! You’ll receive an SMS text with the confirmation details—you can add it to your calendar in one click, or reschedule if you need to.

Is there anything else I can help you with?

Really glad you called. Jay’s looking forward to it. Have a great rest of your day. Bye!
